title: Return policy page found
question: Can an agent find and read the return policy?
method: Follow home-page links whose text or URL matches return, refund, Widerruf, retour or similar, or MerchantReturnPolicy.merchantReturnLink. Pass when the page is fetchable and carries more than 100 words of text; warn when it is shorter; fail when none is found. Every checkout programme (Google Merchant Center and UCP, the OpenAI feed, Stripe, Shopify channels) asks for a return policy URL.

spec.title: Google Merchant Center: shopping ads policies (contact and policy requirements)

title: Shipping policy page found
question: Can an agent find shipping costs, regions and delivery times?
method: Same link heuristics for shipping, delivery, Versand, livraison. Pass when the page is fetchable and mentions regions, costs or delivery times.

title: Privacy policy and terms found
question: Are the privacy policy and terms of service linked and fetchable?
method: Look for the WordPress privacy page link, link text matching privacy, Datenschutz, terms, AGB, conditions. Pass when both pages are fetchable.

title: Merchant identity
question: Who is selling, where are they, and how can they be reached?
method: Pass when Organization JSON-LD (name, address or contactPoint) exists, or an imprint or about page carries a legal name and address.

title: Contact channel
question: Can an agent or its user find a way to contact the merchant?
method: Pass when the home page links a mailto: address, a tel: number, or a same-origin contact or support page; warn when only a cross-origin contact link exists; fail when none. Google Merchant Center requires a contact method on the site, and UCP onboarding asks for at least one.

spec.title: Google Merchant Center: shopping ads policies (contact and policy requirements)

title: Policy pages are agent-readable
question: Can an agent actually read the policy pages it found?
method: For each policy page found (returns, shipping, privacy, terms), require HTTP 200, more than 100 words of text outside scripts, and no robots.txt rule that disallows the search and assistant crawlers of A2.2 on its path. Pass when all found pages qualify; warn when some do not, or when a page carries noindex (reachable for every fetcher, but kept out of the indexes that ground AI answers, as Shopify policy pages are by default); fail when none qualifies. Skip when no policy page was found.

title: security.txt
question: Does the site publish a security contact?
method: Informational. GET /.well-known/security.txt. Pass on a text document with Contact: and Expires: fields whose Expires date is in the future; warn when a field is missing or expired; fail when absent. Operational maturity, not agent readiness: reported, never scored.
